2RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions RBI Grade B 2026 Phase 1 - Reasoning Recollected Questions Directions (1-5) - Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Eleven boxes – M, N, O, P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, and W are kept one above another in a single stack, but not necessarily in the same order. Only one box is kept between M and R. W is kept three boxes above M. The number of boxes kept above W is the same as the number of boxes kept below V. Not more than one box is kept above W. R is not kept seven boxes above V. Only three boxes are kept between M and S, which is not kept immediately above W. The number of boxes kept between T and V is a perfect cube. More than two boxes are kept between T and R. No box is kept between U and Q. Only three boxes are kept between O and Q. The number of boxes kept between N and O is same as the number of boxes kept between M and R. N is placed above P, and there are at least two boxes below P. Q1. How many boxes are between N and P? A. Three B. Two C. One D. None E. More than Four Q2. Which of the following statements is/are true with respect to the final arrangement? A. Only one box is above Box N B. No box between Box P and Box Q C. Box R is kept at fifth from the bottom D. Box P is kept immediately above Box S E. Box U is kept at second from the top Q3. Four of the following five are alike in a certain way as per the given arrangement and hence forms a group. Find the one which doesn’t belong to that group. A. R – S B. W – N C. V – Q D. N – U E. P – O Q4. Which among the following box is fifth from the bottom? A. Box Q B. Box N C. Box P D. Box R E. None of these

3RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions Q5. What is the Position of Box N? A. Third from the bottom B. Fifth from the bottom C. Third from the top D. Second from the top E. Sixth from the bottom Directions (6-50) - Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Seven persons, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, were born in different years among 1953, 1961, 1964, 1970, 1975, 1982 and 1990. Each person belongs to a different place among Delhi, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata and Jaipur. All the information is not necessarily in the same order. The age of each person is calculated from the base year 2026. The one who belongs to Delhi was born immediately after the person whose age is a multiple of 13. Two persons were born between A and the one who belongs to Delhi. No person was born between A and the one who belongs to Jaipur. B was born immediately before the person whose age is a multiple of 17. The sum of the ages of C and the one who belongs to Mumbai is 116. The number of persons born before C is two less than the number of persons born after the one who belongs to Pune. F was born after C but before B. A does not belong to Hyderabad. The number of persons born before the one who belongs to Kolkata is one less than the number of persons born after the one who belongs to Chennai. G was born in a year which is a multiple of 5 but was not born immediately after B. D was born after the one who belongs to Kolkata. Q6. Who was born immediately before the person who belongs to Mumbai? A. The one who belongs to Chennai B. F C. G D. The one who belongs to Pune E. The one who was born immediately after C Q7. If B’s son is 25 years younger than B, in which year was B’s son born? A. 1995 B. 1990 C. 2001 D. 1985 E. 1998 Q8. What is the sum of the age of G and the one who belongs to Hyderabad? A. 95 B. 101 C. 112 D. 108 E. None of these

5RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions Q13. Statements: T ≥ U > M > G; G ≥ F ≤ Y; P < U > V ≥ J ≥ Y Conclusions: I. U > F II. M > J III. G < V A. Only conclusion I follows B. Only conclusion II follows C. Only conclusions Il and III follow D. None follow E. Only conclusion I and II follows Directions (14-19): Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Eight persons – A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H live on eight different floors of an eight-storey building where the lowermost floor is numbered as one, the one above that is numbered as two and so on till the topmost floor is numbered as eight. Only one person lives on each floor. They like different fruits, viz., Grapes, Orange, Mango, Papaya, Banana, Apple, Kiwi and Pineapple. D lives on an odd-numbered floor below floor number six. The one who likes Apple lives two floors above D. Only two people live between the one who likes Apple and the one who likes Papaya. As many persons live below the one who likes Papaya as above H. E, who likes Mango, lives immediately above H. Neither C nor B likes Papaya, and C does not live below B. The one who likes Pineapple lives four floors below the one who likes Grapes. The number of persons living between the one who likes Mango and the one who likes Apple is two less than the number of persons living between C and B. G lives above F, but not immediately above. The one who likes Orange lives above the one who likes Kiwi, but not above the one who likes Banana. Neither the one who likes Orange nor the one who likes Banana lives on an odd- numbered floor. A does not like Apple Q14. Four of the following five are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and thus form a group. Which one of the following does not belong to the group? A. C – Mango B. A – Banana C. B – Pineapple D. G – Papaya E. H – Apple Q15. As many as the floor above the one who likes Pineapple as below ___? A. The one who likes Grapes B. The one who likes Banana C. The one who likes Mango D. The one who likes Kiwi E. The one who likes Apple

Three people live between C and E III). A likes orange and lives on an even-numbered floor A. Only I B. Only II C. Only III D. Both I and II E. Both I and III Q17. How many people live below the one who likes bananas? A. Three B. More than five C. Five D. Six E. Four Q18. Which of the following statements is true with respect to the final arrangement? A. The number of people lives above E same number of people lives below D B. Two floors are between H and F C. G lives immediately above the one who lives three floors below the one who likes Grapes D. F lives on an odd-numbered floor E. G likes Orange Q19. On which floor does the one who likes Kiwi live? A. Second Floor B. Third Floor C. First Floor D. Sixth Floor E. Fifth Floor Q20. If in the word PRECAUTIONS, all vowels are changed to the next letter and all consonants are changed to the previous letter as per the English alphabetical series. After that, all repeated letters and vowels are deleted, then how many consonants are there between the letter which is 2nd from the left end and the letter which is 3rd from the right end? A. 2 B. 3 C. 4 D. 5 E. None of these

7RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions Directions (21-24): Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Maya starts from point A and moves 10 m towards the west to reach point B. From point B, she takes a right turn and moves 8 m to reach point C. Then, she takes a right turn and moves 15 m to reach point D. From point D, she takes a left turn and moves 6 m to reach point E. Finally, she takes a left turn and moves 5 m to reach point F. Priya starts from point L, which is 18 m south of point A. From point L, she moves 12 m towards the west to reach point M. Then, she takes a right turn and moves 15 m to reach point N. After that, she takes a right turn and moves 20 m to reach point O. Finally, she takes a left turn and moves 9 m to reach point P. Q21. What is the direction of point F with respect to point O? A. Northeast B. Northwest C. South D. North E. Southwest Q22. What is the total distance between Point F and Point L? A. 33m B. 28m C. 37m D. 32m E. 24m Q23. Four of the following five are alike in a certain way based on the given arrangement and thus form a group. Which one of the following does not belong to the group? A. FP B. CO C. NL D. FD E. NA Q24. What is the shortest distance between O and C? A. √445m B. √442𝑚𝑚 C. 21m D. √458 m E. None of these

8RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions Directions (25-27): Study the following statements and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows from the given statements disregarding the commonly known facts. Q25. Statements: Some Pen is Copy. Only Copy is Pencil. Only a few Book is Pen. Some Book is Rough. Conclusions: A. Some Pencil being Book is a possibility B. Some Book is not Pen C. All copies being Pen is a possibility D. Some Rough is not Pen E. No Copy is Rough Q26. Statements: All Delhi is Goa. Only a few Jaipur is Surat. Only a few Surat is Delhi. Some Shimla is Jaipur. Conclusions: A. All Shimla is Delhi B. Some Jaipur is Goa C. No Delhi is Surat D. Some Goa is Delhi E. Some Surat is not Jaipur Q27. Statements: Only a few Laptop is Computer. No Keyboard is Laptop. Some Keyboard is Bottle. Only a few Mobile is Computer. Conclusions: A. Some Bottle being not Laptop is a possibility B. No Mobile is Laptop C. All Computer is Keyboard D. Some Mobile is Keyboard E. Some Keyboard being Computer is a possibility

9RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions Directions (28-33): Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below. Eight persons, namely A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre, but not necessarily in the same order. Each person likes a different natural place among Lake, River, Mountain, Forest, Desert, Valley, Island and Beach. The number of persons sitting between F and C is the same as the number of persons sitting between the one who likes Beach and E. The one who likes Lake sits opposite the one who likes Beach. F sits second to the left of the one who likes Beach. B sits immediately to the left of the one who likes River. The one who likes Mountain sits immediately to the right of the one who likes River. Only one person sits between B and the one who likes Island. C sits immediately to the left of the one who likes Island. G sits immediately to the right of the one who likes Beach. The one who likes Desert sits second to the right of the one who likes Island. The one who likes Valley sits immediately to the right of the one who likes Beach. A sits immediately between the one who likes Mountain and the one who likes Valley. H sits adjacent to the one who likes Forest. Q28. Who among the following people likes Forest? A. G B. H C. B D. C E. F Q29. Four of the following five are alike in a certain way based on the final arrangement and hence form a group. Which one does not belong to that group? A. A – Lakes B. D – Island C. F – Forest D. B – Valley E. H – Lakes Q30. Which of the following statements is/are not true? I. The one who likes Island sits immediately to the right of the one who likes Forest. II. B sits third to the left of the one who likes Forest. III. The one who likes Mountains sits second to the right of the one who likes Lakes. A. Only I B. Only II C. Only III D. Both II and III E. All I, II and III

14RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions Directions (47-49) In each of the following questions, a statement is followed by three assumptions numbered I, II and III. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted. Read the statement carefully and decide which of the given assumptions is/are implicit in the statement. Q47. Statement: The bank has advised customers to update their mobile numbers and email IDs in their accounts. This will help them receive transaction alerts, security messages and important account-related updates on time. Assumptions: I. Some customers may not have updated their latest contact details with the bank. II. Customers who update their contact details will get higher interest on deposits. III. Timely alerts can help customers remain informed about account activities. Which of the above assumptions is/are implicit? A. Only III B. Only II C. Both II and III D. Both I and III E. All I, II and III Q48. Statement: The state government has launched a mobile app to help citizens register complaints related to damaged roads, poor street lighting and garbage collection. The complaints will be forwarded directly to the concerned local department. Officials have been instructed to update the complaint status within a fixed time limit. Assumptions: I. Citizens may face civic issues that need timely attention from local departments. II. A mobile app can help in faster reporting and tracking of public complaints. III. All complaints received through the app will be solved immediately. Which of the above assumptions is/are implicit? A. Only I B. Only II C. Both I and II D. Both II and III E. All I, II and III Q49. Statement: A hospital has started an online appointment system to reduce crowding at the registration counter. Patients can book their preferred time slot through the hospital website or mobile app. The hospital has also kept a separate help desk for patients who are unable to use the online system. Assumptions: I. Online appointments can help in reducing crowding at the hospital registration counter. II. Some patients may not be comfortable using the online appointment system. III. Patients booking appointments online will receive free medical consultation. Which of the above assumptions is/are implicit?

# Page 21^page=21
17RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions Directions (54-55) - Read the following paragraph carefully and answer the questions given below. Paragraph: A smartwatch company recently marketed its new smartwatch as a reliable and high- performance product. However, soon after launch, many customers posted negative reviews regarding delayed syncing, inaccurate health readings and sudden device shutdowns. The CEO responded that the complaints were mainly due to a temporary server issue and not because of any defect in the watch. Later, an independent technology analyst reviewed the product and stated that both server instability and hardware-related faults were affecting the smartwatch’s performance. Q54. Which of the following should be the most appropriate course of action for the smartwatch company? A. The company should ignore customer reviews because negative reviews are common after every product launch. B. The company should only improve its marketing campaign to rebuild customer confidence. C. The company should accept only the server issue and continue selling the product without any change. D. The company should conduct a detailed technical audit, publicly communicate the issue and offer repair, replacement or software support wherever required. E. The company should stop manufacturing smartwatches permanently. Q55. Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the CEO’s statement? A. The smartwatch was launched with a large advertising campaign across digital platforms. B. Some customers liked the design and display quality of the smartwatch. C. Independent testing showed that the smartwatch continued to give inaccurate readings even when it was used offline without server connectivity. D. The company had faced delivery delays during the first week of the launch. E. The CEO had earlier worked in another technology company. Directions (56-57) - In each of the following questions, a statement is followed by three inferences numbered I, II and III. Read the statement carefully and decide which of the given inferences logically follows from the information given in the statement. Q56. Statement: Several cities have issued heatwave alerts as temperatures remain unusually high for many days. Hospitals have reported more cases of dehydration and heat exhaustion, especially among elderly people and outdoor workers. Local authorities have advised citizens to avoid direct sunlight during afternoon hours and drink enough water. Inferences: I. All citizens will follow the advisory issued by local authorities. II. Heatwaves can create health risks for vulnerable groups. III. Outdoor workers may be more exposed to heat-related illness than people working indoors.

# Page 22^page=22
18RBI Grade B Phase 1 Reasoning Recollected Questions A. Only I B. Only II C. Both I and II D. Both II and III E. All I, II and III Q57. Statement: During the Iran-US war, global markets reacted sharply due to fears of disruption in oil supply routes. Several countries appealed for restraint and asked both sides to return to diplomatic talks. Humanitarian agencies also warned that prolonged conflict could affect civilians and regional stability. Inferences: I. The conflict may have an impact beyond the two countries directly involved. II. Diplomatic talks are being viewed as a possible way to reduce tensions. III. The war has already ended because several countries appealed for restraint. Which of the above inferences logically follows? A. Only I B. Only II C. Both I and II D. Both I and III E. All I, II and III Directions (58) - Read the following statement carefully and choose the conclusion that logically follows from the information given in the statement. Statement: The Reserve Bank of India’s Clean Note Policy aims to ensure that the public receives clean and good-quality currency notes. Banks are expected to sort notes into issuable and non- issuable categories and avoid practices such as stapling or writing on currency notes. Soiled or unfit notes are to be withdrawn from circulation through the banking system. Q58. Which of the following conclusions can be drawn from the above statement? A. The Clean Note Policy is intended to improve the quality of currency notes available to the public. B. Banks are allowed to issue soiled notes if customers agree to accept them. C. Stapling of currency notes helps increase the life of banknotes. D. The policy applies only to coins and not to currency notes. E. RBI has stopped the circulation of all physical currency notes. Directions (59) - Read the following statement carefully and identify the most possible reason behind the situation described. Situation: Several customers have complained that their debit card transactions failed even though sufficient balance was available in their accounts.
